deep.reconstruction:
Folio 65v carries no derivation of its own. The left (main) page is blank. Only faint, illegible bleed-through from the reverse side shows, for example something like '(x - x_1)...' and scattered '= 0' fragments, and none of it can be read reliably.

The strip at the right edge is not part of 65v. It is the cut-off left margin of the facing leaf, which is the 'next page' transcribed separately (dated Juni 1856). Its line starts match that page exactly:
- 'Integr[ation der Gleichung ∂²u/∂p∂q + u = 0]'
- 'u = ∫ ...'
- the boundary-value lines 'q = +0, p > 0', 'q > 0, p = +0', 'q < 0', 'p < 0'
- the second and third integral representations ('u = ...', then 'q = ...', 'q > ...'), with the separating horizontal rules visible
- '∂²u/∂p∂q + u = 0, ∂²u'/∂p∂q + u' = 0'
- 'ω = Σ(-1)^n (p-p')^n (q-q')^n / (Πn Πn)'
- '∫ ∂ω/∂p u dp + ∂u/∂q ω dq'
- '∫_{s,q'}^{s,p'} ...'
- 'u' = ...'
- '∂u'/∂q' = ...'
- '∂²u'/∂p'∂q' = ...'

For context, that facing page solves a Goursat/characteristic problem for the telegraph-type equation u_pq + u = 0 by Riemann's method. The Riemann function is ω = Σ (-1)^n ((p-p')(q-q'))^n/(n!)^2 = J0(2√((p-p')(q-q'))). The solution u' at (p', q') is obtained by integrating the closed-contour Green identity ∮(ω_p u dp + u_q ω dq) = 0 around the characteristic triangle. Nothing on 65v itself can be reconstructed beyond this identification.

results.what: No substantive result on this page (blank verso; the edge strip is the facing page's margin). Context only: the facing page applies the Riemann-function method to u_pq + u = 0, with ω = J0(2√((p-p')(q-q'))).
results.modern_name: Riemann's method / Riemann function for hyperbolic equations (telegraph equation)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, 1860 ('Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite')

deep.surprise_reason: The page is blank apart from illegible bleed-through. The visible edge fragments belong to the facing page, whose content (Riemann's method, 1856 draft) is already well known as Riemann's.

checkable.asserts: The Riemann function ω = J0(2√(pq)) (shown on the facing page) satisfies ω_pq + ω = 0; the expected result is 0.
The series Σ(-1)^n p^n q^n/(Πn)^2 equals J0(2√(pq)); the expected result is 0.
